cells.tense: You are standing in the middle of something you have already made real.
cells.ask: Pick one finished thing you made and say out loud what it cost, before you start the next one.
cells.core:
You are actually done with something. Not finished talking about it, not ready to move on from it, done with it. What started as an idea has become a real thing sitting in the world, and you carry it differently now.

By this point everything the beginning promised is here at once, and that is what makes it heavy. You can hold it without adding to it. Say out loud what one finished thing cost you, and let one other person hear it. The next thing can start from someone who already carried a thing to the end, and that is a different person than the one who set out.
cells.sheetLine: You've made something real, and the weight of it is the point.
cells.verb: carrying what you started to its completed form
cells.place: where what you are becomes visible as it is

cells.tense: You are already living past the end of a thing that hasn't finished yet.
cells.ask: Leave one project half-done on purpose this week and don't explain it to anyone.
cells.core:
You are pushing ahead of your own completion. The finish line is out in front of you and you have mentally arrived there while your hands are still on the last stretch. From there, everything looks like a delay.

What this looks like steady is slower and duller than you expect. One thing gets finished at the pace it actually takes, and you are in the room while it closes — present for the last stretch, not ahead of it. The pressure has turned the final step into a formality you resent. Let one thing sit half-finished without deciding what it means, and look at it again without the future already written over it.

cells.tense: You have not yet picked up what your own making turned into.
cells.ask: Show one thing you made to someone and ask what they see, then say nothing else.
cells.core:
You made something and then left it standing there. At some point it stopped being yours to hold, and since then you have not been in the room with it. The work is waiting, not for more effort, but for you to receive what it became without deciding what it means first.

Steady here is a plain rhythm: something gets made, then looked at, then made again. That rhythm has stalled, and effort alone will not restart it. Letting someone else tell you what they see does not need you to feel certain first. Receiving can restart there, one outside impression at a time, with your eyes on it before your verdict is.

cells.tense: You have been steering toward what you already are, but you never called it that.
cells.ask: Name one thing you have been calling luck or timing and say, out loud, that it came from you.
cells.core:
You are already becoming what you are, and you have been describing it as something else. Things you built get talked about like they arrived on their own. The steering is happening. What is not happening is anyone saying it was yours.

Steady, the same motion carries the name attached: you choose, you make, you say that you chose and made. That word is not something to add on top. It is missing from the account you give. Put it back on one thing, however small, and let the next step be taken by someone who knows how they got here.
cells.sheetLine: You've been arriving at yourself and calling it something else.
